name: FontPair
tagline: A browsable gallery of Google Fonts pairings with live previews, so you stop guessing which heading goes with which body text.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The product is a preview surface over a font library that is already free and already has a public API. An agent can pull the Google Fonts metadata, render heading plus body specimens in a two-column grid, and give you filters for serif, sans, display and mono in an afternoon. The part you cannot generate is the editorial call that Playfair over Source Sans looks intentional and Lobster over Comic Neue does not, so you seed a starter list of known-good pairs and grow it yourself. For a solo designer or a dev picking type for one project, a local pairing playground with a favorites list is genuinely enough. This is a bookmark that happens to charge money, not infrastructure.
coreLoopDIY: A local page that loads the Google Fonts catalog, shows live heading-and-body specimens for a curated or randomized pair, and lets you filter, shuffle, favorite and copy the embed snippet.
requirements: A Google Fonts Developer API key in .env, or a checked-in copy of the catalog JSON
Node 20 for the tiny static server
A browser, because the whole thing is client-side rendering
whatYouLose: Human curation: someone with taste already threw out the 95 percent of combinations that look bad
Category browsing by vibe or use case rather than by mechanical font classification
Anything beyond Google Fonts, so no commercial or foundry typefaces
Pairing suggestions that account for x-height, weight availability and optical size instead of just family names
Whatever else lives behind the paid tier, since a gallery usually bundles extras like downloadable kits or templates
moatNotes: Curated taste is a real asset and a hard one to fake, but it is also a list you can copy by looking at it once.
whyPeopleStillPay: Most people never pay for this, they just use the free gallery and leave. The ones who do are paying to skip the part where they audition forty combinations at 11pm and pick the wrong one, which is a legitimate purchase of taste-by-proxy. A DIY build gets you the mechanism instantly but not the judgment, and if you already knew which pairs were good you would not have visited the site.
notes: The hard part of a font pairing site was never the code, it was someone with an eye saying no about four hundred times.
prompt:
Build a local font pairing playground as a static single-page app. No accounts, no backend database, no telemetry.

Stack: plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript modules. One tiny Node 20 script (server.js, node:http only, zero dependencies) that serves the folder on localhost:5173 and proxies one endpoint, /api/fonts, to the Google Fonts Developer API using GOOGLE_FONTS_API_KEY from .env. Ship .env.example. If the key is missing, fall back to a checked-in data/fonts-fallback.json snapshot of about 200 popular families with category and available weights, and show a dismissible banner explaining the fallback.

Features, all in scope:
- Seed data/pairs.json with 40 hand-written pairings, each with heading family, body family, and a one-word mood tag. Load it on boot.
- Main view: a full-width specimen card showing a headline, a subhead, and three paragraphs of lorem, rendered in the current pair. Load the two families dynamically by injecting a Google Fonts link tag.
- Controls: two searchable dropdowns (heading font, body font) filtered by category serif, sans-serif, display, handwriting, monospace. Sliders for heading size, body size, body line-height and body measure in characters.
- Shuffle button that picks a random pair, weighted to prefer entries from pairs.json over fully random combinations.
- Favorite button that stores pairs in localStorage, plus a favorites drawer to reload or delete them.
- Copy button that emits the exact HTML link tag and matching CSS font-family declarations for the current pair.
- Editable specimen text: make the headline and body contenteditable so users can paste their own copy.
- Light and dark preview toggle that only affects the specimen area.

Out of scope: uploading local or commercial fonts, user accounts, sharing links, screenshot export, any pairing algorithm smarter than category heuristics.

Keep total CSS under 200 lines, no framework, no build step. Write a README with setup in five lines or fewer and one paragraph saying the curation quality is on the user, not the code.
